picks.excerpt: Strada 2.0 and Strada Connect stitch distributed media libraries together and route AI workflows across globally scattered post teams, a peer-to-peer answer to where footage and models actually live.
picks.rationale: A concrete answer to the distributed-post problem — media stays where it lives and AI workflows travel to it, which changes how remote teams hand off tomorrow.

picks.excerpt: James Cameron's Lightstorm Vision has acquired Outsyders, whose AI-driven stereoscopic conversion pipeline delivered 3D versions of Lilo & Stitch and IMAX's Blue Angels, folding machine-assisted 2D-to-3D into an in-house production stack.
picks.rationale: Machine-assisted 2D-to-3D conversion moves from vendor service to in-house pipeline at the studio that defined modern stereo — a signal for where conversion work goes next.

picks.excerpt: Colorfront brought an automated timeline comparison engine and Dolby Vision 2 mastering to IBC, automating the version-checking drudgery that eats mastering hours.
picks.rationale: Automated version comparison plus Dolby Vision 2 mastering hits the exact hours colorists and QC lose to eyeballing near-identical deliverables.

picks.excerpt: You don't have to use AI in your film — but proving you didn't is becoming its own production task, as provenance metadata and C2PA-style credentials move into the filmmaking workflow.
picks.rationale: Provenance is turning into a deliverable: a practical read on what filmmakers now have to capture and sign, whether or not they touch generative tools.

picks.excerpt: A full-length AI-generated Odyssey lands in front of critics, and the review is a concrete inventory of where generative video still breaks down across 2.5 hours of continuity, performance and pacing.
picks.rationale: The longest stress test yet of generative video — a shot-by-shot map of where continuity, performance and pacing still collapse at feature length.
